policies.title: Named nationalities: Bosnia and Herzegovina general citizen visa exemption
policies.summary: Current state-agency guidance expressly lists these nationalities under its general citizen visa-exemption schedule, rather than its separate ordinary-passport-agreement, diplomatic/official, or business-passport sections.
conditions: The cited schedule is a general citizenship exemption. This normalized ordinary-passport row is limited to a passport presented by a citizen of the named state; it does not transfer the exemption to a diplomatic, official, service, business, identity-card, seaman, emergency, refugee, alien or other special travel document.

The general statutory visa-free ceiling is up to 90 days in a six-month period from first entry, unless an applicable treaty or Council of Ministers decision provides otherwise. This grouped current schedule does not establish a different uniform duration for every nationality.
Work, residence, transit, admissibility, passport validity, carrier and final-border-control requirements remain separate.

policies.title: Malaysia ordinary passports: Bosnia and Herzegovina visa-free agreement route
policies.summary: Current state-agency guidance explicitly places valid Malaysian ordinary passports in its concluded-agreements visa-free section.
conditions: This route is expressly limited to a valid ordinary Malaysian passport under a concluded agreement; it does not establish treatment for diplomatic, official, service, business, identity-card, seaman, emergency, refugee, alien or other special travel documents.
The general statutory visa-free ceiling is up to 90 days in a six-month period from first entry unless the applicable agreement or a Council of Ministers decision provides otherwise.
Work, residence, transit, admissibility, passport validity, carrier and final-border-control requirements remain separate.

policies.title: Brazil ordinary passports: Bosnia and Herzegovina visa-free entry with annual cap
policies.summary: The live Brazilian Presidency decree promulgates the bilateral agreement: nationals holding valid national passports are visa-exempt for tourism, holidays or business for up to 90 days, capped at 180 days annually from first entry.
conditions: The agreement covers nationals of either party who hold valid national passports. This normalized row is limited to a Brazilian ordinary/national passport and does not extend the route to a diplomatic, official, service, business, identity-card, seaman, emergency, refugee, alien or other special travel document.
A stay may not exceed 90 days and the total length of stay may not exceed 180 days per year from first entry.

The treaty is stated to be valid indefinitely but permits diplomatic suspension or denunciation. The cited live legal record does not itself establish that no later diplomatic notification has occurred; final admission remains with Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities.
Work, residence, transit, admissibility, passport validity, carrier and final-border-control requirements remain separate.

conflicts.explanation: The current state-agency schedule expressly limits Hong Kong's exemption to a business passport. It does not establish the same route for an ordinary Hong Kong SAR passport, so the visa-free fallback is not promoted.

unresolved.reason: Current state-agency guidance explicitly grants a visa exemption to holders of Hong Kong business passports, not an ordinary Hong Kong SAR passport. No current state-authority source reviewed maps an ordinary Hong Kong passport to the same route.
